sonnet.problem: This statement re-asks the fact card 2 already asked. Card 2's answer is that the birthright went to Joseph's sons, and 5:1 says Reuben is therefore not reckoned by birthright. Card 4 only asks whether Reuben is still counted by birthright.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The summary card for the 5:3-8 genealogy goes item by item. It names Reuben's four sons and the places Aroer, Nebo and Baal-meon, and it also covers the line down to Beerah and his exile.
sonnet.rule: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

sonnet.problem: This is an ordinary story card with three sentences. It carries three beats: occupying the land until the exile, Manasseh being numerous and where they settled, and the family heads.
sonnet.rule: Every other story card, including the first card of a later stop, is 1 to 2 sentences.

sonnet.problem: The statement tests two claims at once: that the unfaithfulness was turning to the gods of the peoples of the land, and that God had destroyed those peoples before them. It also mostly restates the verse 25 fact card 17 just asked.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.
